LESSON: CAPACITY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.4: Capacity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Capacity, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you measure capacity using arbitrary units?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Measure capacity of containers using a 1 litre container in real life situations in purposive pairs or groups. Those with poor motor coordination or missing limbs could also use assistive technology or be supported by peers ot teacher to carry out the activity.

2. Make 1⁄2 litre containers from locally available materials

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Measure capacity of containers using a 1 litre container in real life situations in purposive pairs or groups. Those with poor motor coordination or missing limbs could also use assistive technology or be supported by peers ot teacher to carry out the activity.
2. Make 1⁄2 litre containers from locally available materials

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Capacity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: as learner makes 1⁄2 litre containers from locally available materials through filling and

emptying the container with substances such as water or sand using a one litre container.

• Self-efficacy: learner shows confidence in measuring capacity of 1⁄2 litre and 1⁄4 litre.

Values:
Responsibility: learner makes 1⁄4 litre containers from locally available materials through filling and emptying

the container with substances such as water or sand using a one litre container.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Learner observes precautionary measures as they determine 1⁄2 litre and 1⁄4 litre containers to enhance

safety.

• Learner uses 1⁄2 litre containers from locally available materials to enhance environmental education.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate practical activities involving measurement of liquids to properties of matter in Science

and Technology.
